transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-10-21
- Time: 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET
- Duration: ~53 minutes
- Platform: Zoom (recording)
- Attendees (Redwood): Elena Park, Mason Liu, Ravi Patel
- Attendees (Arcadia Labs): Samantha Reyes, Ian Cho, Leah Morgan, Tom Bennett

Summary:
Quick planning sync to align North America webinar localization, timing, and retargeting/ad promotion cadence for a co-branded developer-focused webinar targeting product & platform engineers in late November. Focus on regional send times, language fallbacks, subject-line testing, and retargeting flows for attendees/registrants.

Topics covered:
- Regional scheduling and capacity for NA time zones
- Localization scope (which locales, copy vs captions vs fully localized landing pages)
- Subject-line and content A/B experiments
- Paid media retargeting plan and CRM integration
- Assets and deadlines for QA and rehearsal

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Elena Park: alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick roll call — can everyone say hi and their role so we stay aligned?
[00:07] Samantha Reyes: yeah hi Samantha Reyes here, I run developer relations at Arcadia. thanks for setting this up.
[00:11] Ian Cho: Ian Cho, growth marketing at Arcadia.
[00:13] Leah Morgan: Leah, localization lead. excited to talk locales.
[00:15] Mason Liu: Mason from Redwood events, hi.
[00:17] Ravi Patel: Ravi on content, good morning.
[00:19] Tom Bennett: Tom — paid media. quick note, will probably ask about retargeting windows later.

[00:22] Elena Park: great. goal for this call is super practical — pick timezone windows, agree on the localization depth, and set the split tests for subject lines and CTAs so we can hit production deadlines. we have, I think, about five weeks until target run date so timelines are tight.

[00:35] Samantha Reyes: five weeks sounds right. our timeline's: we want a rehearsal 1 week before and final asset freeze three days before. also need to confirm if captions can be live and whether we can host the landing page localized or use query params.

[00:48] Mason Liu: platform can do live captions in english natively, we've done machine captions for other locales but need to validate accuracy. hosting localized landing pages is fine but it adds a little ops overhead. alternative is locale-aware query params that swap copy at render.

[00:58] Leah Morgan: query params are fine for small changes but for fr-CA we often need full copy edits because legal localization and bilingual headers. for en-CA and en-US it's small differences but fr-CA requires full page.

[01:10] Elena Park: good call. so proposed priority locales: en-US, en-CA, fr-CA, es-US. keep others as english with translated captions. Leah ok with that?

[01:17] Leah Morgan: yes that's workable. I'll need the final marketing copy length constraints and the hero phrase so translations can be scoped.

[01:22] Ravi Patel: i'll produce hero phrases and three different CTAs — sign up + reminder, sign up + demo CTA, and sign up + whitepaper follow up. we'll test which performs better for developer audiences.

[01:32] Ian Cho: for audience segments, we want current trial users, API users with 30–90 days activity, and a broader lookalike. we'll run an email to existing users and a paid push for lookalikes, then retarget registrants who don't attend with a three-touch sequence.

[01:45] Tom Bennett: for paid, we typically do a 14-day retarget window for registrants then shrink to 7 for non-responders; do you want us to do 14->7 or something else?

[01:54] Samantha Reyes: Ian and I prefer 14->7 cadence, but also we want to cap frequency to avoid spamming devs. maybe 2 impressions/day max.

[02:02] Elena Park: noted. Mason, can the webinar platform support a 14-day registration pixel + two separate retargeting audiences (registered but not attended, visited landing but not registered)?

[02:11] Mason Liu: yes, we can surface both audiences to your ad accounts. need your CRM audience IDs for mapping and to confirm the pixel domain.

[02:17] Ian Cho: i'll dump audience IDs into the sheet after this call.

[02:20] Elena Park: perfect. subject-line testing — Ravi, what are you thinking? short code-y subject lines or value-driven headline?

[02:25] Ravi Patel: for dev audience, we should test three buckets: technical hook (e.g., "Reducing LLM latency by 3x"), product outcome ("Cut inference costs for production"), and curiosity ("What top scale teams do differently"). we'll do 20/60/20 split and track CTR and registration conversion.

[02:40] Samantha Reyes: i like the technical hook and curiosity for our community. we should localize the technical hook carefully — numbers and acronyms don't always translate.

[02:48] Leah Morgan: correct — numbers are fine but the phrasing around "latency" may need a local equivalent, i'll look into appropriate terms in fr-CA.

[02:56] Elena Park: good — Leah, please create a short glossary for terms we must not translate versus terms to localize. that'll help consistency across assets.

[03:03] Leah Morgan: will do.

[03:05] Mason Liu: logistics question — rehearsal: do we want a dry-run with panelists and slide deck, or a tech-only run?

[03:09] Samantha Reyes: panel run is valuable, especially for timing of demo. we want full run-through plus 15 minutes for Q&A simulation.

[03:16] Elena Park: ok schedule a full panel rehearsal, tech check one day prior. Mason, can you pencil rehearsal at 1 week before?

[03:21] Mason Liu: yes, I'll propose slots for each region — likely two rehearsal times to catch east and west coast participants.

[03:25] Ravi Patel: about assets — how many variants for social ads do we need? 2 hero images + 2 copy lengths per locale?

[03:31] Tom Bennett: we recommend 2 hero images and 3 copy cuts (30, 90, 200 char) so we can test short caption vs longer description. also need CTA buttons localized.

[03:41] Elena Park: sounds good. marketing automation flow — Ian, what's your preferred post-registration cadence? immediate confirm, reminder 24h before, 1h before, and post-webinar follow-up with recording?

[03:49] Ian Cho: yes immediate and a 24h reminder. we usually do a 2-step post follow-up: recording + short survey, then an educational nurture 3 days later.

[03:56] Samantha Reyes: and for registrants who don't attend, send the recording in 24 hours but keep the subject simple — "Recording: [title]".

[04:02] Elena Park: agreed. also want a short callout in the recording email for "Request a demo" for high-intent leads. RavI, can you create that copy?

[04:07] Ravi Patel: yes, short demo CTA and a link to request time.

[04:09] Elena Park: competitors — anyone worried about other vendors co-marketing around the same time?

[04:14] Samantha Reyes: we've seen Anthropic do a developer webcast the same week in the past; we can work around timing and promotion windows.

[04:18] Leah Morgan: also keep an eye on Hugging Face event calendars; we don't want to clash with major community conf days.

[04:24] Mason Liu: ok will check public event calendars and propose dates that avoid major vendor webcasts.

[04:28] Elena Park: risk register quick pass — what could derail this? locales missing copy, platform caption glitches, and ad account pixel mismatches. any others?

[04:36] Ian Cho: stakeholder availability — if Arcadia speakers have product freeze or holidays that week could be an issue. I will map internal blackout dates.

[04:42] Elena Park: final piece: measurement and KPIs. primary: registrant count and registration->attendee rate, secondary: qualified leads created (demo requests), and paid conversion from retargeting. revenue influence tracked by CRM tags.

[04:55] Samantha Reyes: ok that KPI set works. can you add a small dashboard in the Redwood console so we can see token-level costs and landing conversion?

[05:02] Elena Park: yes we can add a simple dashboard and share a read-only view.

[05:06] Mason Liu: i'll add rehearsal invites and the runbook to the shared folder.

[05:09] Elena Park: awesome. recap of next steps: Elena will share subject-line matrix and send the regional time-slot spreadsheet, Leah will deliver localization glossary and localized taglines, Mason proposes rehearsal times, Ian dumps audience IDs, Tom sets paid media cadence, Ravi drafts CTAs and promo cuts. We'll reconvene in 1 week for a quick check.

[05:26] Samantha Reyes: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:29] Elena Park: thanks team, talk soon.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]
